title: C melody versus tenor, and whether C melody has any jazz use
summary: Cobb explains that moving from C melody to tenor was easy apart from the key; the Danceses ask about the C melody's sound and Kenny Davern, and he calls it a marching band horn.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Well, now, Arnett, going from C melody to tenor, that wasn't as simple as that, was it?
Yeah.
It was?
Very simple to me. Because the mechanism of the situation was the same. The only difference was the
key signature.
Yeah.
C melody is a C horn just like piano. But the tenor is a B flat instrument --
Yeah.
-- which is, as you know, a tone above the piano.
Right.
ALL RIGHT, But that doesn't make any difference what your key instrument is, as long as it's an instrument that you can play in jazz.
Well --
But C melody, they don't use it in jazz bands.
NO: (Unintelligible)
But, see, I didn't know that then either. I found all this out later. Isn't that something how you can learn later on? Helen, don't look at me in that tone of voice.
C melody, though, it kind of can sound pretty, can't it?
I think it can sound pretty, but, see, I never really concentrated on it after I left it. Now, I'm talking about the '30s now, Stanley, and that's a long time ago. Now, if you bring me one today --
Yeah.
-- I'll let you know more about it because I have more knowledge about what's going on.
Well, I was wondering, you know, what -- you know, I really don't know much about the C melody.
Well, does it sound anything like the soprano saxophone?
It's between the soprano and the alto, isn't it?
Yeah.
But what I really meant was, doesn't it have a kind --
May I tell you something?
Yeah.
It's strictly for marching band, that's all it's for.
Oh, I see.
That's all it is.
No, but I wondered whether it had a character of its own which was -- there's somebody who's playing that now -- oh, you know that boy, the clarinet player, Kenny DAVERN?
Yeah.
I think he's playing a C melody now.
Yeah, I READ THAT somewhere (unintelligible)
Who is that?

There was a boy called Kenny DAUSBN, plays clarinet; they had what they called Soprano -- he and BAB Wilbur were both playing soprano (Soprano Summit+--ed.) saxophones. And somebody told me that he was playing C melody. I just wondered what sort of sound he'd get on it.
C melody could be maybe a beautiful instrument, but it's not a known instrument to jazz musicians today. And nobody's ever thought of it. It could be an instrument maybe today that might be superb.
